newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's SNCF chooses Cegetel as telecoms partner.
newsitem.headline: France's SNCF chooses Cegetel as telecoms partner.

text.p: France's SNCF state railway has chosen Generale des Eaux unit Cegetel as its industrial partner to run its telecommunications network, a spokesman said on Wednesday.

SNCF's board met Wednesday to decide on a partner from a list of suitors that also included France's Bouygues and its Italian partner Stet and a consortium called Unisource backed by companies in the Netherlands, Switzerland, Sweden, Spain and possibly the United States.
Cegetel is a joint venture between Generale des Eaux, British Telecom Plc and Mannesmann of Germany.

An SNCF statement released afterwards said negotiations to finalise the arrangement with Cegetel would be completed by March 31. It said the final choice had been between Cegetel and Bouygues and its aim now was to seal a definitive accord with the company that made the best offer.
SNCF searched for a partner after French Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon in December granted a 15-year telecoms operating licence to its Telecom Developpement unit.

The SNCF licence covers the railroad's existing network of 8,000 kilometres of optic fibre all over the country, as well as radio links, which will be expanded to some 12,000 kilometres in the next six years, SNCF sources have said.
